item.title: Are Westlaw Headnotes Like Banana Costumes?
item.description: No decision has a stronger claim to being this year’s worst copyright decision than the Third Circuit’s precedential opinion in Thomson Reuters v. ROSS. Though the case ostensibly involves two legal research companies, the court’s ruling could broadly impact authors’ ability to use facts and ideas that first appeared in existing works.

item.title: Authors Alliance files amicus brief in In re OpenAI Copyright Infringement Litigation
item.description: On October 29, Authors Alliance asked the court for leave to file an amicus brief in In re OpenAI, Inc. Copyright Infringement Litigation, the consolidated copyright lawsuits against OpenAI and Microsoft pending in federal court in New York. Our brief supports the defendants' motions for summary judgment, but focuses onone issue only: whether "market dilution" is a kind of harm that copyright law recognizes. We argue that it is not, and that treating it as one would end up hurting many of the authors the theory claims to protect.
